observations.body: Josiah destroys vessels, priests, high places, child-sacrifice sites, horses, altars, and images, then commands a Passover unmatched since the judges.
observations.label: Josiah removes rival worship and restores Passover

observations.body: The passage presents temple cleansing, removed priests, desecrated sites, ended child sacrifice, destroyed altars, covenant book, and Passover as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: temple cleansing, removed priests, desecrated sites, ended child sacrifice, destroyed altars, covenant book, and Passover

observations.body: The passage places reform and passover beside temple cleansing, removed priests, desecrated sites, ended child sacrifice, destroyed altars, covenant book, and Passover.

payload.posture: Read 2 Kings 23:4–25 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the reform joins destruction and restoration without claiming later kings remain faithful
